title: Primary spinal bone tumors presenting as foraminal nerve sheath lesions: illustrative cases.
summary: Dumbbell-shaped foraminal lesions are usually benign nerve sheath tumors, but primary bone tumors can adopt the same silhouette. When they do, preoperative imaging is often misread as a schwannoma and oncological therapy is delayed. Five patients (2 women, ages 25-66 years) had cervical (n = 2), thoracic (n = 2), or lumbosacral (n = 1) lesions interpreted as benign nerve sheath tumors on MRI. On CT, available in 4 cases, each lesion showed cortical breach or expansile lysis that had not altered the initial diagnosis. Final pathological analysis revealed vertebral hemangioma (n = 2), giant cell tumor of bone (n = 1), synovial sarcoma (n = 1), and undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (n = 1).

We present a patient with longstanding drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy, in whom high-titre serum anti-GAD65 Abs were identified during evaluation for epilepsy surgery, with subsequent marked improvement in seizure burden following treatment with corticosteroids, immunoglobulin, rituximab, and mycophenolate mofetil. title: Gazing Upon the Great Eye: A Rare Presentation of Behcet's Disease.
summary: Behcet's disease is a systemic autoimmune condition presenting classically with recurrent and painful mucocutaneous ulcers. We report the case of a 41-year-old female who presented with left-sided pan-uveitis, shifting hypopyon, and retinitis. title: A Multi-Modal Posterior Network for Memory Retrieval From Visuospatial and Olfactory Context.
summary: Retrieval of context-dependent episodic memories is thought to rely on a temporo-parietal network comprising hippocampal, parahippocampal, retrosplenial, and posterior parietal cortices. However, although real experiences occur within rich multi-modal contexts, and computational models emphasize convergence zones and the need for cross-modal binding, experimental evidence from humans predominantly relies on a single contextual modality (often visual). title: How Perceived Traits Modulate the Neural Processing of Reward During Reinforcement Learning.
summary: Humans infer others' traits through positive and negative feedback, and these perceived traits, in turn, shape how individuals perceive others' behavior. Although previous studies have investigated the neural basis of reward and trait learning, the temporal dynamics by which trait-level learning signals modulate reward-related brain responses during learning remain poorly understood. title: Treadmill Walking Differentially Modulates Early Auditory Responses to Standard and Deviant Sounds.
summary: People often encounter environmental sounds while walking without attending to them, but it is unclear whether walking alters early cortical responses to these sounds. We recorded 32-channel electroencephalography from 22 healthy young adults during a passive auditory frequency-oddball paradigm. Conditions were sitting and treadmill walking without an object, with a water-filled cup or with a clay-filled cup matched for mass and apparent fill height. title: Opportunistic Central Nervous System Infections and Graft Outcomes in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
summary: Opportunistic central nervous system (CNS) infections represent a source of morbidity and mortality among solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. Clinicians must balance effective pathogen-directed treatment against risks of allograft rejection versus progression of infection. In this study, we defined the epidemiology and outcomes of CNS infections, including their impact on graft survival. summary: Oscillating steady-state imaging (OSSI) is an fMRI acquisition technique that utilizes a novel oscillating steady-state by combining balanced gradients and quadratic RF phase cycle to achieve a higher SNR compared to spoiled GRE. Despite its SNR advantage, OSSI is sensitive to fluctuations in the B 0 field due to respiration and drift, which limits the achievable SNR gains. title: Guillain-Barré/Miller Fisher Overlap Syndrome Associated With Listeria monocytogenes Peritonitis During Chemotherapy for Ovarian Cancer: A Case Report.
summary: Guillain-Barré/Miller Fisher overlap syndrome (GBS/MFS overlap syndrome) is an acute immune-mediated polyneuropathy characterized by features of Miller Fisher syndrome, including ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and decreased tendon reflexes, accompanied by limb weakness. We report a case of clinically diagnosed GBS/MFS overlap syndrome occurring in association with Listeria monocytogenes peritonitis during chemotherapy for high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). title: White Matter Geometric Disorganization Links Subcortical Degeneration to Motor Impairment in Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3.
summary: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3) is the most common hereditary ataxia caused by CAG repeat expansion in the ATXN3 gene. However, the structural mechanisms linking genetic burden, neurodegeneration, and motor impairment remain poorly understood. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 105 genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 133 healthy controls. Diffusion MRI and structural MRI were acquired using harmonized protocols and harmonized across sites using ComBat. title: Reduced Functional Connectivity Between the Precuneus and Prefrontal-Insular Regions in Atopic Dermatitis: A Resting-State fMRI Study.
summary: This resting-state functional MRI (R-fMRI) study investigates brain functional alterations associated with atopic dermatitis (AD), a chronic itchy skin condition, using two partially overlapping cohorts scanned approximately 2 years apart. title: Transient global amnesia with a characteristic hippocampal lesion following mild traumatic brain injury: a case report.
summary: Transient global amnesia (TGA) is characterized by sudden-onset anterograde amnesia lasting up to 24 hours, accompanied by variable retrograde amnesia. summary: To quantify brain-wide morphometric similarity network (MSN) reorganization in temporal-lobe glioblastoma on post-treatment MRI and relate it to lesion burden and longitudinal change. summary: Angelman syndrome (AS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder associated with loss of maternal UBE3A function in neurons. We report a 30-month-old Chinese boy with global developmental delay, motor impairment, and severe expressive language impairment, without clinically observed seizures during the available follow-up. title: Cerebral Infarction As the Presenting Feature of Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2) V617F-Positive Polycythemia Vera: A Case Report.
summary: Polycythemia vera (PV) is a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm driven predominantly by the Janus kinase (JAK)2 V617F mutation and characterized by an absolute increase in red cell mass. title: ATLAS-FREE FUNCTIONAL BRAIN CONNECTOME ANALYSIS VIA TASK-DRIVEN PARCELLATION.

summary: Functional brain connectome analysis models brain connectivity as a network, where nodes represent brain regions and edges capture their functional interactions. title: Molecular Diagnosis of Rickettsial Meningoencephalitis With Concurrent Herpes Simplex Virus Type 2 Infection in a Young Female Presenting With Acute Febrile Encephalopathy: A Report on a Rare Case.
summary: Rickettsial CNS infections have been increasingly reported in tropical countries, including India, and are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Early diagnosis is challenging due to nonspecific presentations, absent rash/eschar, and limited sensitivity of conventional serological tests in the acute phase. Concurrent CNS infection with herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) is exceedingly rare and further complicates clinical diagnosis and management. title: Spatial regularisation for improved accuracy and interpretability in keypoint-based registration.

summary: Unsupervised registration strategies bypass requirements in ground truth transforms or segmentations by optimising similarity metrics between fixed and moved volumes. title: Baló-Type Inflammatory Pseudotumoral Lesion Mimicking a Cerebral Metastasis: A Diagnostic Challenge.
summary: Baló's concentric sclerosis is a rare inflammatory demyelinating disorder characterized by concentric layers of demyelinated and relatively preserved myelin. Its clinical and radiological presentation may mimic an intracranial neoplasm, particularly when a solitary enhancing lesion is associated with diffusion restriction. We report the case of a 34-year-old woman who presented with acute right-sided motor symptoms involving the lower limb and fine movements of the right hand. title: Cortical spreading depression on Riemannian 2-manifolds: eikonal-curvature analysis and sulcal trapping.
summary: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. title: Incidental Metastatic High-Grade Neuroendocrine Carcinoma Diagnosed by Liver Biopsy During Cholecystectomy: A Case Report.
summary: Neuroendocrine neoplasms range from relatively indolent well-differentiated tumors to aggressive poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). A 70-year-old woman developed nausea, vomiting, and epigastric abdominal pain several weeks after pelvic reconstructive surgery. title: Sex-Specific Myostatin-Grey Matter Volume Associations in Ageing Adults: Implications for the Muscle-Brain Axis.
summary: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for cognitive decline, suggesting bidirectional muscle-brain crosstalk mediated by myokines. Myostatin, a negative regulator of muscle growth, may influence brain health through systemic signalling, yet human neuroimaging evidence remains lacking. summary: The 2024 revision of the McDonald criteria expands the role of paraclinical evidence to expedite multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis while aiming to preserve diagnostic accuracy. title: Longitudinal ACC Alterations with Low-Dose Pregabalin in pBMS.
summary: Primary burning mouth syndrome (pBMS) is a chronic orofacial pain disorder in which the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) serves as a core node in descending pain modulation and central sensitization. Multiparametric MRI evidence for structural, metabolic, and functional abnormalities across ACC subregions remains limited. This single-arm, prospective longitudinal study characterized ACC subregional alterations in 38 patients with moderate-to-severe pBMS and 31 matched healthy controls. All patients received a standardized 4-wk low-dose pregabalin course, with clinical and neuroimaging measures reassessed posttreatment; 30 of 34 patients who completed the trial provided posttreatment MRI data.

summary: To investigate whether voxel-wise multiparametric physiologic MRI-based tumor habitat analysis captures intratumoral heterogeneity that differentiates non-enhancing glioblastoma (GBM) from low-grade glioma (LGG) beyond clinical and conventional imaging features. title: Influence of regional white matter lesion volume differences related to cardiorespiratory fitness on cognition in healthy older adults.
summary: Greater cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) has been associated with reduced global burden of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) lesions, a neuroimaging marker of small vessel cerebrovascular disease, and lower risk of age-related cognitive impairment and dementia. title: Late cortical dynamics mediate numerosity illusions induced by symmetry.
summary: Numerosity perception enables us to quickly estimate the number of objects in a visual scene, a fundamental skill supporting efficient interaction with the environment. title: Foundation model-enhanced multimodal survival prediction in glioblastoma across multi-institutional cohorts.
summary: MRI foundation models (FMs) have shown potential for improving performance of neuroimaging tasks, but their value specifically in Glioblastoma overall survival risk prediction remains unclear. title: Sex-related differences in striatal functional connectivity in early Parkinson's disease.
summary: A sex-specific pattern within the dopaminergic pathways may underlie the clinical divergences between male and female patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) over the disease course. summary: Bruns syndrome is a rare manifestation of intraventricular neurocysticercosis characterized by intermittent cerebrospinal fluid obstruction through a ball-valve mechanism. summary: The neural mechanisms of multiple-item working memory are not well understood. summary: The astringency surface sub-quality is pivotal to red wine perception, yet its neural bases remain unclear. title: Neuroimaging Profiling of Residual Ischemic Risk in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Acute Ischemic Stroke.
summary: Predicting recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation remains a clinical challenge, as traditional risk scores such as CHA2DS2-VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes, previous stroke or transient ischemic attack, vascular disease, age 65 to 74 years, and sex category) often fail to account for the mechanistic insights provided by brain imaging. title: Alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats: effects of age of onset and drinking severity.
summary: Adolescents' heightened reward sensitivity has been suggested to contribute to increased risky drinking during this developmental period compared to adulthood. title: Individual differences in blood-brain barrier permeability are associated with childhood trauma and circulating immune markers in major depressive disorder: Preliminary findings.
summary: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a major public health challenge, and childhood trauma is an important risk factor for its development. title: Effects of Mindfulness Training on Impulsivity and NoGo-Go-Related Brain Activation in Internet Gaming Disorder.
summary: This study aimed to determine whether the effects of mindfulness meditation training (MMT) on impulsivity and Internet gaming disorder (IGD) severity operate through sequential or parallel pathways, and to identify the neural correlates associated with these effects. summary: Accumulating evidence implicates dopaminergic dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet direct evidence of such dysfunction and of its altered coupling with the functional connectome remains limited. summary: Although previous studies have reported abnormal hippocampal volumes in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the specific alterations in hippocampal subfields and their relationships with clinical symptoms in high-functioning ASD (HF-ASD) remain unclear. title: Plasma proteomic signatures in incident multiple sclerosis.
summary: This study aimed to identify plasma proteomic signatures associated with multiple sclerosis (MS) prior to clinical diagnosis and to determine whether prioritized proteins are related to multimodal markers of neurodegeneration and tissue injury. title: Safety of Peri-procedural antithrombotic agents in magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy.
summary: Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) thalamotomy is an increasingly used, minimally invasive alternative to deep brain stimulation (DBS) for essential tremor and tremor-dominant Parkinson disease. title: Predicting the naturalistic course of obsessive-compulsive disorder during two-year follow-up in adolescence.
summary: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) during adolescence follows heterogeneous trajectories, from remission to persistence. title: Intranasal embelin-nanostructured lipid carrier with β-cyclodextrin inclusion complex (EBCD) produces sustained behavioural control of convulsive activity in the lithium-pilocarpine rat model: A behavioural and neurochemical comparison with intranasal diazepam.
summary: Status epilepticus (SE) is a neurological emergency requiring rapid behavioural control of convulsive activity. title: Childhood emotional neglect modulates emotional face processing in healthy young adults: An ERP study.
summary: Childhood Emotional Abuse (EA) and Emotional Neglect (EN) have been proposed to have long-term effects on emotion processing and their neurophysiological correlates in a wide range of clinical populations, yet evidence from non-clinical samples remains limited. summary: Friedreich ataxia (FRDA) causes motor disability through combined proprioceptive deafferentation and cerebello-cortical dysfunction. summary: To integrate normative modeling with non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) to characterize individualized brain functional abnormalities across Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), thereby elucidating disease heterogeneity and enabling biologically informed stratification. summary: Persistent impairment of consciousness after sedation withdrawal represents a diagnostic and prognostic challenge in critically ill patients, particularly in the absence of major structural brain injury. title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals

summary: Motor decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) supports non-invasive brain-computer interfaces, yet existing methods either rely on costly cue-based trials and coarse categorical labels or use pretraining objectives that do not directly capture how movement unfolds, limiting their ability to learn transferable motor representations.
